dialect.detail: Student project likely compiled with GnuCOBOL or similar PC-based COBOL; uses Windows file paths (C:\COBOL\), ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL, and FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE consistent with COBOL-85/2002 features available in GnuCOBOL
evidence: ASSIGN TO UT-SYS-INVFILE with WS-FILES PIC X(76) VALUE 'C:\COBOL\outDAT.txt'

purpose.domain_detail: Student project (university course) sorting a sales file by client number and producing a formatted report
purpose.summary: Reads a sequential sales input file, sorts records by client number in ascending order using a SORT verb, then reads the sorted file and writes a formatted report with headings, detail lines, and a footer showing totals for sales tax and final sale. Handles pagination with a line counter.

notable_features: SORT verb with SD, USING, GIVING
Pagination logic with LINE-COUNT and FULL-PAGE-COUNT
Formatted PICTURE clauses with currency symbols (-$,$$$.99, -$$,$$9.99)
File path literals stored in WORKING-STORAGE (WS-FILES)
verdict.notes: Program authored by Derek R Schultz and Andre J Sandoval, dated April 2018, clearly a student project. Footer has typos ('TOAL SALES TAX' instead of 'TOTAL'). Windows-style file paths suggest PC-based GnuCOBOL or Micro Focus Personal COBOL environment. No lines exceed 72 characters confirming fixed format. The WS-CUR-DATE structure maps CURRENT-DATE in YYYYDDMM order which appears to swap day and month fields (CUR-DAY at positions 5-6, CUR-MONTH at 7-8) — a likely student bug.
